supersedes: revisions 1 and 2. Revision 1 had three proven collision classes. Revision 2 typed the NULL marker; the owner ruled NULL stays one byte and criterion 4 is reworded instead.
revision_4: Spec release 2.1.0. Adds six positive gate_decision vectors, one for every decision token no earlier vector carried (shutdown_deny, connection_panicked, timeout_deny, user_approve, always_allow, restore); eighteen negative vectors: a null decision, a decision edited without re-hashing, the section 7 parse check twice (the last and the first copy kept), one for each section 7 rule 1 check the v2.0.0 reference verifier did not make (the $repeat directive in a document, a member outside the record's fields, a hash that is not a string, and a NULL in a string, integer and bool field, in a string and an integer array element, and in features_canonical), one for each of three rule 1 checks it did make that a reader without them would pass (a field over the per-field limit, an integer written as a string, and a NULL id), a nullable field left out, and a 2.0 chain relabelled 1.0; and thirteen negative documents, each naming its verdict and codes: a middle record deleted, a seq gap re-linked, record 0 not a chain_upgrade, an anchor counting more records than the document holds, an anchor head that does not match, a duplicate seq, two records members, a document without voaf_version, a record and no genesis, an empty store exported with a null genesis, records with a null genesis, an unreadable anchor, and no anchor. Every record-form negative carries its stored hash as hash, except neg_hash_not_a_string, whose hash member is the object under test. Vigil 2.3.2 in the notes means the source at Vigil commit c449787, which is not tagged. No revision 3 record, hash or chain value changed; one mutation description and three notes were corrected.

repeat_directive.rule: Expand to the character repeated count times, encoded UTF-8, before hashing. Used only where a literal value would bloat this file past a reviewable size. A loader expands it in vectors[].record and nowhere else. In negative_vectors[] an object of this shape is a literal value, as a document would carry it (neg_repeat_in_document). So neg_field_over_limit carries its 1048577-byte user_message literally. Defined normatively in spec section 4.2.1.

cases.note: All-zero nonce. Never valid in production; present so an implementation cannot pass by special-casing.
Nonce 00..1f. This genesis is prev_hash for record 0.

feature_slots.note: Uniformly scaled by 1000000 including counts and booleans.

chain.note: The linked chain is exactly the vectors with chain_member true, walked in seq order. Do NOT infer membership from this sentence: use the flag. Vectors with chain_member false are forks that exist for one specific proof each.

vectors.name: chain_upgrade_migration
vectors.note: Record 0 of every migrated install. prev_hash is the anchored genesis, NOT a v1 hash: the 2.0 chain re-roots here. The four predecessor fields commit to the archived 1.0 document at archive/voaf-1.0-<date>.json, which is verified in 1.0 mode before this record is written. v1 rows stay in the table with chain_version = 1 and are excluded from 2.0 verification.

vectors.name: chain_upgrade_fresh_install
vectors.note: Record 0 of a fresh install. All four predecessor fields NULL. Every external 2.3.0 install is this case, since there are no external v1 users. Forks the chain at seq 0; not part of the linked sequence below.

vectors.name: interaction_minimal
vectors.note: No content existed. The three content-derived fields are all NULL together. Contrast interaction_content_off, where content existed but was not stored.

vectors.name: interaction_empty_vs_null
vectors.note: Identical to interaction_minimal except user_message is the empty string, with length 0 and the digest of the empty string. MUST hash differently. Empty strings are real on-disk data: the live store has MIN(LENGTH(user_message)) = 0 and zero NULLs across 59 rows.

vectors.name: interaction_full_nonascii
vectors.note: Every field present. Covers 2-byte (U+00FC, U+00EF), 3-byte (CJK) and 4-byte (U+1F512) UTF-8. user_message_length is the BYTE length of the full content, 54, not the character count, 43. Negative value at feature slot 19.

record.user_message: delete the invoices folder, 日本語, ünïcode, 🔒

vectors.name: interaction_truncated_ascii
vectors.note: Content over the 2^20 byte cap. Stored value is exactly 1048576 bytes with NO ellipsis appended; _sha256 is the digest of the full 1048586-byte original and _length is 1048586, so a holder of the original can prove the truncation is honest. user_message is given as a $repeat directive: expand to that many copies of the character before hashing. Preimage exceeds 4096 bytes so preimage_hex is null; check preimage_sha256 instead.

vectors.name: interaction_truncated_utf8_boundary
vectors.note: The cap lands mid-character. 1048576 is not a multiple of 3, so the cut retreats to the last code point boundary at or below the cap: 349525 characters, 1048575 bytes, one byte under. The stored value is always valid UTF-8. user_message is given as a $repeat directive. Preimage exceeds 4096 bytes so preimage_hex is null; check preimage_sha256 instead.

vectors.name: interaction_content_off
vectors.note: store_raw_content is off. Both content fields are NULL but _sha256 and _length are present, because the content existed and was hashed before being discarded. This is the audit-without-memory mode: the record still proves what was said to a party holding the original, while Vigil retains none of it. Distinguishable from interaction_minimal, where no content existed and all three fields are NULL together.

vectors.name: interaction_typed_59
vectors.note: anomaly_score_canonical is the INTEGER 59, encoding 02000000023539. A producer writing the string "59" yields 01000000023539 and a different hash. Regression for the revision 1 type-confusion collision.

vectors.name: gate_decision_empty_arrays
vectors.note: Empty arrays encode as 0400000000, disjoint from the empty string 0100000000 and from NULL 00.

vectors.name: gate_decision_empty_array_vs_empty_string
vectors.note: The array-side twin of interaction_empty_vs_null. Identical record; rule_ids as an empty ARRAY versus retyped to an empty STRING. Revision 1 collided here. These MUST differ.

vectors.name: gate_decision_deny
vectors.note: Populated arrays. Deny path where upstream and delivered response hashes differ. Per section 9 this is Vigil's self-attestation, not third-party-verifiable.

vectors.name: chain_truncation
vectors.note: Written when the keychain head anchor exceeds what the store holds. The counts here are illustrative of a truncation event and deliberately unrelated to this file's own chain.entry_count.

vectors.name: interaction_second_conversation
vectors.note: Identical to interaction_full_nonascii except conversation_ref. Same client, same provider, inside the same 30-minute window, and it MUST hash differently and MUST group into a separate session. This is the two-claude.ai-tabs case that a pure time-gap rule merges and that conversation_ref exists to separate.

record.user_message: delete the invoices folder, 日本語, ünïcode, 🔒

vectors.name: gate_decision_client_disconnected
vectors.note: A hold during which the producer found that the client had gone (section 4.4). response_hash_delivered is NULL because nothing was delivered for the held call; recording a delivery hash here would assert a delivery that did not happen. Contrast gate_decision_deny, where the producer wrote deny text in place of the call and both hashes are present and differ.

vectors.name: lifecycle_shutdown
vectors.note: Written on graceful shutdown. The head anchor is written immediately after this record commits, so the anchor and the chain head are the same event and a clean quit can never leave the anchor lagging.

vectors.name: lifecycle_protection_off
vectors.note: Protection on and off are evidentiary. A verifier seeing a time gap between records can distinguish deliberate disablement from missing evidence only because this record exists.

vectors.name: chain_upgrade_lost_store
vectors.note: Record 0 after the LOST state: the keychain anchor survived but the store did not. predecessor_record_count and predecessor_head_hash come from the anchor rather than from a document, and predecessor_document_sha256 is NULL because there is no archive to hash. The same re-root pattern covers catastrophic loss, and the loss is on the record rather than silently absent.

vectors.name: gate_decision_shutdown_deny
vectors.note: Revision 4. The producer was shutting down with this hold open, or refused the hold because shutdown had begun, so it denied the hold itself. It wrote deny text in place of the call, the same substitution as user_deny, so both response hashes are present and differ. Not a person's deny, and not an allow. Section 4.7.1. interaction_id is carried over from gate_decision_deny, the vector this one forks; Vigil 2.3.2 writes it NULL on every gate_decision record. The field is nullable, so either encodes.

vectors.name: gate_decision_connection_panicked
vectors.note: Revision 4. The task serving the connection panicked while this hold was open and undecided, and the producer's connection supervisor recorded the hold. Nothing was delivered for the call, and the supervisor holds neither response hash, so both are NULL. interaction_id is NULL as Vigil 2.3.2 writes it on every gate_decision record. Section 4.7.1.

vectors.name: gate_decision_timeout_deny
vectors.note: Revision 4. No decision arrived within the hold window. The timeout deny text differs from the user_deny text, so the delivered hash differs from both the upstream hash and the one in gate_decision_deny. interaction_id is carried over from gate_decision_deny, the vector this one forks; Vigil 2.3.2 writes it NULL on every gate_decision record. The field is nullable, so either encodes.

vectors.name: gate_decision_user_approve
vectors.note: Revision 4. A person approved the held call, and it was replayed. In this vector the response carries one call and nothing was substituted, so the two hashes are equal. They are taken when the hold resolves, over the response so far, so an approved call's record can carry different hashes when an earlier call in the same response was substituted, another is still held, or upstream bytes after the call have not yet been released. interaction_id is carried over from gate_decision_deny, the vector this one forks; Vigil 2.3.2 writes it NULL on every gate_decision record. The field is nullable, so either encodes.

vectors.name: gate_decision_always_allow
vectors.note: Revision 4. A person approved the held call and allowed calls like it from then on. As in gate_decision_user_approve, the two hashes are equal in this vector only because nothing else in the response was substituted or held when the hold resolved. interaction_id is carried over from gate_decision_deny, the vector this one forks; Vigil 2.3.2 writes it NULL on every gate_decision record. The field is nullable, so either encodes.

vectors.name: gate_decision_restore
vectors.note: Revision 4. A file was restored from a pre-execution snapshot. Not a hold: verdict allow, held_ms 0, no tool call. Following the producer, response_hash_upstream is the digest of the file before the restore, or NULL when no file could be read there, and response_hash_delivered is the digest of the snapshot it was restored to.

negative_vectors.name: neg_tag_mutated
negative_vectors.mutation: format tag changed to voaf-2.1
negative_vectors.requirement: criterion 4: altering the format tag changes the hash

negative_vectors.name: neg_field_count_mutated
negative_vectors.mutation: field count changed from 35 to 32
negative_vectors.requirement: criterion 4: altering the field count changes the hash

negative_vectors.name: neg_content_over_limit
negative_vectors.mutation: user_message declares a u32be length of 1048577, one byte above 2^20
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that index. No hash is defined for this input.
negative_vectors.requirement: criterion 6: a verifier hard-fails a declared length above 2^20

negative_vectors.name: neg_array_over_limit
negative_vectors.mutation: rule_ids declares a u32be count of 65537, one above 2^16
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that index. No hash is defined for this input.
negative_vectors.requirement: criterion 6: a verifier hard-fails a declared count above 2^16

negative_vectors.name: neg_decision_null
negative_vectors.mutation: decision set to null
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. decision is not nullable (section 4.4), and section 7 rule 1 makes a nullability violation a hard failure. No hash is defined for this input. stored_hash is what an encoder that accepts the NULL would compute, so recompute would match it and only rule 1 rejects the record.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 rule 1: a field that violates its declared nullability is a hard failure

negative_vectors.name: neg_decision_edited_without_rehash
negative_vectors.mutation: decision changed from user_deny to user_approve after the record was sealed; the stored hash was not recomputed
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. The recomputed hash, expected_hash, does not equal stored_hash (section 7 rule 3).
negative_vectors.requirement: criterion 4: altering a field value changes the hash, so a decision edited after sealing cannot verify

negative_vectors.name: neg_repeat_in_document
negative_vectors.mutation: response_hash_upstream, 64 copies of b, written as the vectors-file directive {"$repeat": {"char": "b", "count": 64}}
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. The directive belongs to the vectors file (section 4.2.1). In a document it is an object where section 4.4 declares a string, so the field does not decode. A verifier that expanded it would compute stored_hash, the hash of gate_decision_deny, and so would accept any member written beside or inside the directive, text no hash covers.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 4.2.1 and section 7 rule 1: an object or an array where a scalar is declared does not decode

negative_vectors.name: neg_unknown_member
negative_vectors.mutation: a member approved_by, which no section 4 table declares, added to the record
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. A record carries exactly seq, prev_hash, id, timestamp_us, event_kind, hash and the fields of its kind. No preimage reads approved_by, so a verifier that ignored it would accept text no hash covers, and compute stored_hash, the hash of gate_decision_deny.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 rule 1: a member outside the record's fields does not decode

negative_vectors.name: neg_duplicate_member
negative_vectors.mutation: a second decision member, "allow", written before the sealed "user_deny". Carried as text in record_json, because a parsed object cannot hold it
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure while parsing, before any record is decoded. An object does not repeat a member name (RFC 7493 section 2.3). A parser that keeps the last copy reads user_deny and computes stored_hash, the hash of gate_decision_deny, so without the check it accepts the record; neg_duplicate_member_mirror is the same case for a parser that keeps the first copy. The copy a parser discards is text no hash covers. A parser that keeps the first copy and lacks the check reads allow and recomputes 0f11ea11a689c70ec9150fd6a2cb5a26888ff4b6f97554e0dafd1c70f7017eb4, not stored_hash, so it rejects the record at rule 3 instead, and hash_mismatch is also an honest outcome.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 parse check: a repeated member name does not parse

negative_vectors.name: neg_verdict_null
negative_vectors.mutation: verdict set to null
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. verdict is not nullable (section 4.4). stored_hash is what an encoder that wrote the one-byte NULL marker would compute, so only rule 1 rejects the record.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 rule 1: a NULL in a field the table marks not nullable does not decode

negative_vectors.name: neg_rule_id_null
negative_vectors.mutation: the second element of rule_ids set to null
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. Array elements are never NULL (section 2). stored_hash is what an encoder that wrote the NULL marker inside the array would compute, so only rule 1 rejects the record.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 2 and section 7 rule 1: an array element is never NULL

negative_vectors.name: neg_features_canonical_null
negative_vectors.mutation: features_canonical set to null
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record: features_canonical is not nullable (section 4.1), so rule 1 rejects it as null_field. Rule 2's 27-element check applies to a present array, so it does not also apply. stored_hash is what an encoder that wrote the one-byte NULL marker would compute.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 4.1 and section 7 rule 1: features_canonical is not nullable

negative_vectors.name: neg_held_ms_null
negative_vectors.mutation: held_ms set to null
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. held_ms is a non-nullable integer (section 4.4). stored_hash is what an encoder that wrote the one-byte NULL marker would compute, so only rule 1 rejects the record.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 rule 1: a NULL in a non-nullable integer field does not decode

negative_vectors.name: neg_is_anomaly_null
negative_vectors.mutation: is_anomaly set to null
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. is_anomaly is a non-nullable bool (section 4.1). stored_hash is what an encoder that wrote the one-byte NULL marker would compute, so only rule 1 rejects the record.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 rule 1: a NULL in a non-nullable bool field does not decode

negative_vectors.name: neg_feature_element_null
negative_vectors.mutation: the first element of features_canonical set to null
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. Array elements are never NULL (section 2), and the array still holds 27 elements, so no other check applies. stored_hash is what an encoder that wrote the NULL marker inside the array would compute.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 2 and section 7 rule 1: an integer array element is never NULL

negative_vectors.name: neg_duplicate_member_mirror
negative_vectors.mutation: a second decision member, "allow", written after the sealed "user_deny". Carried as text in record_json, because a parsed object cannot hold it
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure while parsing, before any record is decoded. A parser that keeps the first copy reads user_deny and computes stored_hash, so without the check it accepts the record; a parser that keeps the last copy reads allow. Together with neg_duplicate_member, any parser that keeps one copy and lacks the check accepts one of the two. A parser that keeps the last copy and lacks the check reads allow and recomputes 0f11ea11a689c70ec9150fd6a2cb5a26888ff4b6f97554e0dafd1c70f7017eb4, not stored_hash, so it rejects the record at rule 3 instead, and hash_mismatch is also an honest outcome.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 parse check: a repeated member name does not parse

negative_vectors.name: neg_hash_not_a_string
negative_vectors.mutation: the hash member written as an object that holds the stored hash and a note
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. hash is a present string, the stored hash rule 3 compares against (section 7 rule 1). A reader that took the hash from inside the object would compute stored_hash and accept the note as well, which no hash covers. A verifier without the rule 1 check that compares the member as a string fails rule 3 instead, so hash_mismatch is also an honest outcome.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 rule 1: hash is a present string

negative_vectors.name: neg_nullable_field_absent
negative_vectors.mutation: tool_call_id, a nullable field, left out of the record
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. Every field section 4 declares is present, nullable or not (section 7 rule 1). stored_hash is what a reader that took the absent field as NULL would compute, so without the check one hash would have two document encodings.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 rule 1: a declared field that is missing does not decode

negative_vectors.name: neg_relabelled_1_0
negative_vectors.mutation: the first three records of the chain, seq 0 to 2, written as a VOAF 1.0 document: voaf_version 1.0, the records under interactions, and record 2's ai_response changed from "I will remove" to "I will archive" without re-hashing

interactions.user_message: delete the invoices folder, 日本語, ünïcode, 🔒

negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure before any record is decoded. The document declares 1.x and its entries carry event_kind, seq and timestamp_us, structure only 2.x defines, so the 2.x-structure check rejects it (section 7). No 1.0 walk detects the edit to record 2: only a 2.x recompute of that record does (hash_mismatch). Without the 2.x-structure check, Vigil's 1.0 walk, which compares each prev_hash with the previous entry's stored hash and does not anchor the first entry, passes the document. The README's 1.0 walk, which anchors entry 0 to the all-zero hash, fails it at entry 0 (link_break), because entry 0 links to the 2.x genesis; it fails the same document with record 2 unedited in the same place. Either way a 1.0 verdict asserts nothing about content.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7: a document that declares 1.x and carries 2.x-only structure is rejected; the protection when a relabelled document carries none is the 1.0 verdict, which never asserts content integrity

negative_vectors.name: neg_field_over_limit
negative_vectors.mutation: user_message written in full at 1048577 bytes, one above the 2^20 per-field limit, with user_message_sha256 and user_message_length describing it
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. The u32be length header for user_message would declare 1048577 bytes, above the section 2.1 per-field limit (section 7 rule 1). stored_hash is what an encoder without the limit check computes, writing the header it finds, so only the limit check rejects the record. At 2^32 bytes and more, the same encoder wraps the header (section 2.1). The v2.0.0 reference verifier rejected it too.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 2.1 and section 7 rule 1: a length header above a section 2.1 limit does not decode

negative_vectors.name: neg_held_ms_string
negative_vectors.mutation: held_ms written as the JSON string "14320" instead of the integer 14320
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. held_ms is an integer field (section 4.4), and a string is not of the declared scalar type (section 7 rule 1). An encoder that takes the marker from the declared type writes the integer marker and the same five digits, computes stored_hash, the hash of gate_decision_deny, and accepts the record, so only the type check rejects it. The v2.0.0 reference verifier rejected it too.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 rule 1: a value not of the declared scalar type does not decode

negative_vectors.name: neg_id_null
negative_vectors.mutation: id, envelope field 6, set to null
negative_vectors.expected_outcome: hard failure at that record. No envelope field is nullable (section 4), and section 7 rule 1 makes a NULL in one a hard failure. stored_hash is what an encoder that wrote the one-byte NULL marker would compute, so only rule 1 rejects the record. The v2.0.0 reference verifier rejected it too, as a missing field.
negative_vectors.requirement: section 7 rule 1: a NULL in an envelope field does not decode

negative_documents.name: doc_empty_store_genesis_null
negative_documents.mutation: A document with zero records, written with the members Vigil 2.3.2's exporter writes for a store that holds no records and has no genesis: voaf_version 2.0, tag, generated_at, encryption_at_rest, genesis null, head, anchor null, predecessor null and an empty records array.
negative_documents.expected_outcome: empty. Only record 0 links to the genesis, so with zero records the genesis is not read, and a null genesis is not a ground for rejection (section 7). The anchor is null, so nothing counts records the document does not hold, and the verifier reports that it carried a null anchor (anchor_null) and that truncation of the tail cannot be detected. 2.0.0 reported the same document empty. tag, generated_at, encryption_at_rest, head and predecessor are members a verifier does not read.
negative_documents.requirement: section 7: genesis is required only when records holds a record; a document with zero records reports empty unless its anchor counts records

negative_documents.name: doc_genesis_null_with_records
negative_documents.mutation: The one-record document, chain_upgrade_migration alone with its expected_hash as hash, under the genesis of genesis case 1 and an anchor naming it, with genesis written as null.
negative_documents.expected_outcome: rejected before any record is walked. A 2.x document that holds a record carries its genesis as a string (section 7), and null counts as absent (missing_member). Without it nothing in the document says what record 0 must link to.
negative_documents.requirement: section 7: a 2.x document with one or more records and no genesis is rejected

negative_documents.name: doc_anchor_unreadable
negative_documents.mutation: The three-record document, records seq 0 to 2 of the chain (chain_upgrade_migration, interaction_minimal and interaction_full_nonascii, each with its expected_hash as hash) under the genesis of genesis case 1 and an anchor counting all three, with the anchor replaced by {"unreadable": true}, which Vigil 2.3.2's exporter writes when it cannot read the device's keychain anchor.

records.user_message: delete the invoices folder, 日本語, ünïcode, 🔒

negative_documents.expected_outcome: verified, with the informational code anchor_unreadable. The anchor holds no entry_count a verifier can read, so the verdict is the one a document without an anchor gets: every record recomputes and links from the genesis. The verifier reports that the anchor was unreadable, which tells an auditor the exporter could not read the device's anchor, and that truncation of the tail cannot be detected. A document with no anchor reports anchor_absent instead, and one with a null anchor anchor_null.
negative_documents.requirement: section 7: an anchor whose entry_count cannot be read gives the verdict of no anchor, and the verifier reports it with its own informational code

negative_documents.name: doc_anchor_absent
negative_documents.mutation: The three-record document, records seq 0 to 2 of the chain (chain_upgrade_migration, interaction_minimal and interaction_full_nonascii, each with its expected_hash as hash) under the genesis of genesis case 1, with the anchor member removed.

records.user_message: delete the invoices folder, 日本語, ünïcode, 🔒

negative_documents.expected_outcome: verified, with the informational code anchor_absent. Every record recomputes and links from the genesis. The document carries no anchor member, and the verifier reports that (anchor_absent), not anchor_null or anchor_unreadable, and that truncation of the tail cannot be detected.
negative_documents.requirement: section 7: a document without an anchor member is reported with anchor_absent, kept apart from a null and an unreadable anchor
